stem: Tellurium is an element in Group 16. The most common isotope of tellurium is $^{130}\text{Te}$. Its electronic configuration is $[\text{Kr}]$ $4\text{d}^{10}$ $5\text{s}^2$ $5\text{p}^4$.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text:
Complete Table 1.1.

Table 1.1

|  | nucleon number | number of neutrons | number of electrons |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| $^{130}\text{Te}$ |  |  |  |

parts.label: (b)
parts.text: Identify the sub-shell in an atom of Te that contains electrons with the lowest energy.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text: Construct an equation to represent the first ionisation energy of Te.

parts.label: (d)(i)
parts.text:
The radius of Te ions decreases after each successive ionisation.

State **two** factors that are responsible for the increase in the first six ionisation energies of Te.

parts.label: (d)(ii)
(e)
parts.text:
Te reacts with $\text{F}_2$ at $150^{\circ}\text{C}$ to form $\text{TeF}_x$. Molecules of $\text{TeF}_x$ are octahedral with bond angles of $90^{\circ}$.

Explain why $\text{TeF}_x$ is octahedral with bond angles of $90^{\circ}$.

parts.label: (f)(i)
parts.stem: $\text{TeF}_x$ reacts with water to form tellurium hydroxide and HF. The oxidation number of tellurium does **not** change during this reaction.
parts.text: Construct an equation for the reaction of $\text{TeF}_x$ with water.

parts.label: (f)(ii)
parts.text: Name the type of reaction that occurs when $\text{TeF}_x$ reacts with water.
